brief.headline: Memory sector in bear market—Samsung/Hynix down >20% from highs despite HBM supply lock, hyperscaler capex at $725B
brief.summary: <cite index="47-1,47-7">Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix have fallen more than 20% from recent closing highs, entering bear market territory despite Samsung's record profit estimates.</cite> <cite index="38-8">Samsung Electronics tumbled more than 7% while SK Hynix sank over 9% at the open on July 3rd, wiping out billions in market value.</cite> <cite index="1-2,1-3">HBM3E pricing stands at ~$300/stack with SK Hynix leading at 50-55% market share.</cite> <cite index="15-2,15-13">DRAM contract prices are forecast to rise another 13–18% QoQ in Q3 2026 and NAND up 10–15%.</cite> <cite index="19-6,20-15">Hyperscalers plan to allocate $725 billion to capex in 2026, up 77% YoY.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="1-3,1-9">SK Hynix holds 50-55% HBM market share</cite> vs. <cite index="45-8">Samsung's 35% share as of Q3 2025.</cite> <cite index="36-5,37-3">NVIDIA has secured approximately 60% of TSMC's 2026 CoWoS capacity</cite>, benefiting Hynix given superior HBM qualification status. <cite index="38-11,38-12,38-13">Hynix announced 100 trillion won ($64B) domestic investment: 80 trillion for M17 NAND fab (H1 2029 start) and 20 trillion for P&T7 advanced packaging to meet HBM and enterprise SSD demand.</cite> <cite index="39-1,39-2">Commerce Secretary Lutnick is pressing both firms to expand US memory production.</cite> Samsung lags on HBM3E yields but has diversified revenue across logic/foundry. Relative: long Hynix near-term on HBM allocation edge, but valuation spread compressed after -20% drawdown.

memory_cycle.stage: Late mid-cycle tightness with pricing deceleration
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="12-10">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93–98% QoQ.</cite> <cite index="15-15,16-7">Q2 DRAM rose 58–63% QoQ, NAND 70–75%.</cite> <cite index="15-2">Q3 guidance: DRAM +13–18%, NAND +10–15%.</cite> <cite index="8-1,8-2,8-3">Server DDR5 profitability has overtaken HBM since early 2026—a historic inflection.</cite> <cite index="9-1">HBM prices could more than double in 2027 as Nvidia's Rubin platform drives demand, HBM4 raises production costs, and long-term agreements lock up capacity.</cite> <cite index="15-6,15-43">Capacity relief not expected until late 2027 or 2028; most analysts expect peak in 2027.</cite> Consumer demand destruction evident; enterprise AI remains inelastic.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-2,4-8">HBM now represents 30-40% of AI accelerator BOM; for B200 with eight HBM3e stacks, memory alone costs $2,400, exceeding logic die cost.</cite> <cite index="4-9,4-11">Supply remains constrained through 2026 with lead times for HBM3E stacks at 20-26 weeks.</cite> <cite index="7-1,7-8,7-9">Samsung and SK Hynix hiked HBM3E prices nearly 20% for 2026 deliveries as manufacturers pivot resources toward HBM4, creating supply crunch for current standard.</cite> <cite index="13-11">HBM4 is projected to launch Q3 2026.</cite> <cite index="2-20,2-21">Nvidia has multi-year agreements reportedly accounting for the majority of SK Hynix's HBM output through 2026.</cite> Pricing power intact; allocation economics favor Hynix.

news_pulse.headline: Memory stocks enter bear market: Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron down >20% from June highs
news_pulse.implication: Profit-taking despite structural HBM demand and record Samsung earnings. Sector lost ~$1.5T market cap since June 25. Tests whether good news already priced.

news_pulse.headline: HBM prices set to double in 2027 on Nvidia Rubin demand, HBM4 transition, and capacity lockups
news_pulse.implication: Bullish 2027 ASP outlook as HBM4 raises production costs and LTAs consume greater share of DRAM capacity. Reinforces pricing power thesis.

news_pulse.headline: US Commerce Secretary Lutnick presses Samsung, SK Hynix to expand US memory output
news_pulse.implication: Geopolitical pressure to diversify supply. May unlock CHIPS Act subsidies but requires multi-year capex; near-term supply unaffected.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix announces 100 trillion won ($64B) South Korea investment: M17 NAND fab + P&T7 packaging
news_pulse.implication: M17 NAND fab targets H1 2029 start; P&T7 expands advanced packaging for HBM. Signals confidence in enterprise SSD and HBM server demand.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrows from 20% to 10% by end-2026; capacity to hit 115–140k wpm
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing faster than expected; NVIDIA secured ~60% of 2026 capacity. Benefits AI accelerator shipments, indirectly boosts HBM demand.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 AI capex at $725B, up 77% YoY; Goldman raises 2025–2030 cumulative estimate to $5.3T
news_pulse.implication: Demand side intact. Microsoft ~$190B, Amazon ~$200B, Alphabet $175–185B, Meta $115–135B. Memory and power infrastructure remain constraints.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q3 contract pricing +13–18% QoQ, NAND +10–15%; deceleration from Q2's 58–63% / 70–75% gains
news_pulse.implication: Rate of increase slowing but direction unchanged. Consumer demand destruction evident; enterprise AI pull remains inelastic. Peak delayed to 2027.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Server DDR5 profitability overtook HBM in early 2026—historic first; CSP LTAs lock floors
news_pulse.implication: Server DDR5 ASP escalation driven by capacity diversion to HBM. LTA floor pricing limits downside; suppliers gain leverage for 2027 HBM rally.

brief.derivatives_signal: No options data in payload. ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) illiquid. KOSPI 200 futures correlation to Nasdaq broke during July 2–3 selloff; local vol premium elevated. Watch put skew on MU as memory ETF (DRAM) proxy—sector down >20% suggests hedging activity. SK Hynix US listing Friday (implied) may provide synthetic vol surface.
